EX57-27.classification: current test defect only; no runtime defect established

original_finding.summary: The incomplete-topic rollback test can reject on cooldown before reaching the intended duplicate post insert, while `.rejects.toBeDefined()` accepts either failure.

post_r5_proof: The current test still creates topic and reply through createHyperdriveForumWriter with a controllable clock that advances by FORUM_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS on each write.
It then constructs a new DrizzleForumRepository with the default forumWritePolicy, whose now() uses the real current clock.

DrizzleForumRepository.createTopicWithInitialPost() calls enforceForumWriteCooldown() as the first operation inside its transaction, before section lookup and before topic/title/post/revision inserts.

The latest reply created by the controlled writer is timestamped ahead of the real clock during a fast run, so the default-clock repository can throw ForumWriteRateLimitError before the duplicate `post-1` insert.
The test still accepts any rejection with `.rejects.toBeDefined()` and then checks only that `atomic-rollback-topic` is absent.
later_pr_disconfirmation: PR #81 does not touch forum repository/write policy/migrations.test rollback evidence.
PR #83–#85 are documentation/audit-state work and do not touch the rollback test or write path.
PR #86 touches tests/database/migrations.test.ts only for the R2 persistent-locale invariant and migration count; the EX57-27 rollback block is unchanged.
PR #87 and #88 affect translation task/bundle remediation only.
PR #89 changes forum presentation/catalog/render tests/styles only and does not touch database rollback evidence.
Current db/forum-repository.ts still runs cooldown before all createTopicWithInitialPost inserts.

defect_proof.controlled_writer_timing: With the current test closure `now: () => new Date(clock += FORUM_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS)`, the topic initial post is created at approximately base+5s and the reply at base+10s.
defect_proof.default_repository_timing: The later default DrizzleForumRepository uses `new Date()` and therefore can observe a latest post timestamp in the future relative to its own clock.
defect_proof.cooldown_formula: retryAfterMs = cooldownMs - (now - latest.createdAt); if retryAfterMs > 0, ForumWriteRateLimitError is thrown.
defect_proof.current_assertion_problem: `.rejects.toBeDefined()` cannot distinguish ForumWriteRateLimitError from the intended PostgreSQL duplicate-key failure. The following topic-absence assertion can therefore prove only that nothing was written before the intended mutation started, not that PostgreSQL rolled back a partially inserted topic graph.

clock_boundary: Keep the existing controlled `clock` shared with createHyperdriveForumWriter.
After the successful reply, advance `clock` by exactly FORUM_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS once.
Construct the rollback-test DrizzleForumRepository with `{ cooldownMs: FORUM_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS, now: () => new Date(clock) }`.
At the intended rollback attempt, `now - latest.createdAt == cooldownMs`, so current repository logic (`retryAfterMs > 0`) deterministically permits the write to proceed beyond the cooldown guard.
selected_future_correction.duplicate_precondition: Before the rollback attempt, assert that `forum_posts.id = 'post-1'` exists and belongs to `topic-1`, making the duplicate primary-key failure an explicit fixture precondition.
failure_assertions: Capture the thrown error rather than accepting an arbitrary rejection.
Explicitly assert that the error is not an instance of ForumWriteRateLimitError.
Under the current Drizzle/node-postgres stack, assert the wrapped PostgreSQL cause has SQLSTATE `23505` (unique_violation).

Assert PostgreSQL constraint identity `forum_posts_pkey`; node-postgres exposes the server constraint field as DatabaseError.constraint and current Drizzle error handling preserves database details in `.cause`.
If the current stack unexpectedly does not expose a stable constraint identity, stop and return to Codex rather than weakening the test to generic rejection.
rollback_graph_assertions: After the intended failure, assert no row exists in forum_topics with id `atomic-rollback-topic`.
Assert no forum_topic_title_revisions row exists with id `atomic-duplicate` (and/or topic_id `atomic-rollback-topic`).
Assert no forum_posts row exists with topic_id `atomic-rollback-topic`.
Assert no forum_post_revisions row exists with id `atomic-body`.
Optionally reassert that the pre-existing duplicate `post-1` still belongs to `topic-1`; this may strengthen fixture clarity but is not required for rollback proof.
selected_future_correction.rationale: This is the smallest correction because it changes only the evidence harness. It exercises the existing transaction unchanged and proves that topic + title rows inserted before the duplicate forum_posts primary-key failure are actually rolled back.

postgres_error_contract.why_primary_key: The intentional duplicate uses existing post id `post-1` with a different new topic id. The composite UNIQUE(topic_id,id) is therefore not duplicated; the duplicate is the forum_posts primary key on id.
postgres_error_contract.repository_evidence: Current database tests already demonstrate that Drizzle query failures preserve PostgreSQL code in the error `.cause`; node-postgres parser maps PostgreSQL field `n` to DatabaseError.constraint.

project_state_decision.reason: R6 changes only the credibility/precision of one PostgreSQL regression test. It does not change runtime behavior, product capability, phase/stage completion, architecture/schema/dependencies/external state, known limitations tracked by PROJECT_STATE.md, or the nearest development route. Current PROJECT_STATE already truthfully states transactional per-author cooldown and local/CI Stage 4 completion.
project_state_decision.stop_if_contrary_evidence: If implementation exposes a distinct runtime transaction defect or otherwise makes a PROJECT_STATE assertion false/materially incomplete, stop and return to Codex; do not add PROJECT_STATE.md automatically.
